text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt and Colombia agree on the important role the non-aligned movement has in pushing forward the peace process. Colombian President Ernesto Samper says he asked Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to exert more effort to push all sides involved in the peace process back to the negotiating table.
- Mubarak issues several directives to improve Luxor airport and reclaim 40,000 acres (16,188 hectares).

- Public Administration Minister Atef Obeid says after returning from Paris that a delegation from the World Bank will arrive in Egypt next week to discuss boosting exports with the relevant ministers. The bank will also offer Egypt $2.5 billion in assistance over the next two years.
- Moroccan officials say that Mubarak and King Hassan will hold meetings on the peace process this month.

- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily says Egypt can export up to $12 billion annually. He says boosting exports is not totally the responsibility of the government but private sector firms must also make an effort.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says: Israel will never have both land and peace. Moussa was speaking in Red Sea resort Sharm el-Sheikh after Mubarak met Samper.
- An Israeli academy to be set up in Arab East Jerusalem.
